_doc: ⚑ THE RESTART CARD — on Daniel's 1997 monitor, lit inside the Close (Sérgio, 2026-09-12: 'We need a way to enter the restart as you option… think of a better idea' → ruled: Daniel's monitor in the Close). Drawn in ERA1's own palette and type because it is that machine speaking, thirty years on, and it is the frame's voice — functional, undecorated. Text is Claude's under the 2026-08-17 norm (docs/reinterp/ERA4_DRAFTS_2026-09-12.md §1); Sérgio's edit wins. `kept` is the one sentence that is TRUE of the piece and FALSE of every apparatus in it — CLAUDE.md's no-storage invariant, said out loud once. No thanks-for-playing, no credits: credits stay in the game menu.

_docDossier: S167 (his 2026-09-21: "if I touch the computer, I should be able to go back to the dossiers") — a button on the card that opens the frame's own reading of the four panels: their status and the practices behind them, each with its source (the menu's The Close — sources). The frame's, not the machine's: the machine offers a way back; the frame says what was done.

receipt._doc: S167 / L-07 (his 2026-09-21: "yes, you can create a receipt of the whole experience") — the version-history receipt, back on the machine as a second face of the card: every update stacked, each FAILED, then the file's lines. Frame voice, in the machine's own till-print. `{n}` entries · `{f}` flagged from the ledger; the practices met, per era, from the record — read, never invented.

receipt._docSearches: ⚑ S193 — the four-era browser's rhyme (PLAN_ROUND5, his 'from early Internet Explorer to modern Chrome'): in 1997 the shame typed the query and the network answered it; in 2026 the machine typed it for her. Read off the ledger: his line only if he searched (search-1997), hers only if 2026's file has begun; the queries themselves are the data's (s1_browser.json query, s4_browser.json program.chosen).

_docSourceButton: ⚑ S177 / R4-30 (his D3, 2026-09-26) — `panelButton` is the era-styled button on each panel's story face (1997 bevel, 2003 Restorify blue, 2016 glass pill, 2026 dark chip; pointCloud.ts drawSourcesButton); `panelHint` says the whole panel still works — the headset's wand presses anywhere. Frame voice.
_docSource: ⚑ S175 (was S174 / R4-18) — THE DOSSIERS ARE ON THE PANELS. S174 opened a room's dossier on Daniel's machine; Sérgio: 'the sources open need to be on the 4 panels that make the Close — it is nuisance to go back and forth. Instead of the computer.' So a press on a panel turns IT to its room's dossier, in that room's own OS (1997 grey on teal, 2003 on Restorify's blue, 2016's glass, 2026's dark), page by page, and back to the room after the last page; a label press opens its room's panel (the seven process labels, which have no room, open on the panel you face, in the frame's own dialog). Content and drawing: src/witness/dossier.ts; the words a visitor reads for the statuses: status_words.json. ⚑ NO PER-LABEL CLAIM IS MADE: a label only carries a name and an era, so its window is its room's dossier with the label marked — opening 'detransition cohort study (Fenway)' onto Era 4's practices under its own name would imply a link the data never makes.
filed: {n} entries were filed under four names, {f} of them flagged.
_docFiled: ⚑ S146 — the one number the whole Witness system was building to, on the last screen, in the frame's flat voice: the file's size, read off the ledger at the moment the card lights (src/witness/record.ts). It sits above `kept`, so the two sentences are read together: this many entries; none kept.
